subject: mcp: sync_tasks endpoint — zero-arg signal triggers lifecycle on session delta, returns judge nudge
description:
Add POST /sync/tasks to the daemon and expose it as an MCP tool (sync_tasks). No request body needed. Behavior:
1. Identifies the calling session (from auth token / session header)
2. Scans ~/.claude/tasks/<session>/ for task files not yet processed (delta since last sync)
3. Runs the native task lifecycle pipeline (embed + blockedBy wires + judge seed) on each new/changed task
4. Returns: { new_tasks: N, blocking_edges_added: M, candidates_queued: K, nudge: "judge_edges" | "idle" }

The nudge field mirrors next_action semantics — if candidates_queued > 0, returns "judge_edges" so the agent knows to dispatch a judge drain immediately without a separate poll.

Agent usage pattern after TaskCreate batch:
  1. TaskCreate × N  (writes native files)
  2. sync_tasks()    (daemon processes delta, returns nudge)
  3. if nudge=="judge_edges" → dispatch judge drain subagent

The fs.watch callback remains as passive fallback for cases where sync_tasks isn't called. This tool can eventually replace the manual suggest_links → add_dependency wiring flow for routine task creation.
